scope: Inference-only English standard diagnostic, not training or a comprehensive model benchmark

validation.runtime_check: passed: readable activity, direct question survives in-flight generation, stale ambient request expires, session duplicate checks retained

conditions.runtime: llama.cpp b12318 Windows CPU x64 (actual instance runtime)
conditions.temperature: 0 in initial training-shaped comparison; 0.6 in ablation and unseen cases
conditions.schema: same constrained action schema as Java; unseen comparison uses speech-only NONE

limitations: Synthetic counterfactual contexts, not a capture of private runtime prompts. latest.log contains delivered speech but does not record the model per reply or its input snapshot.
Ten deliberately varied unseen cases are a small diagnostic set, not a statistically powered leaderboard.
Timings are native HTTP generation without game load, queue, retries or delivery cooldown. Do not compare them directly to total player wait time.
No merged-BF16-versus-GGUF numerical equivalence test was performed; template/masking checks alone do not prove quantization has zero quality cost.
All production duplicate, fact, action and delivery guards remain; these independent model tests do not count extra runtime retries.
findings: Cross-NPC negative wording context causes reproduced topic drift: MiniCPM greeting changes from Hey again lol to No tool rn.
Raw activity translation keys and display-case daily jobs differ from training schema. Readable activities and enum jobs improve controlled work/greeting cases.
Direct requests previously shared five-second queue expiry with ambient chatter, shorter than typical LFM3 inference.
Eight thousand nine hundred nineteen training rows have only 764 distinct context inputs. Ten alternative outputs do not add ten different situations.
All three completed two epochs and used the current training data hash. Low validation loss did not guarantee relevant generated speech on new contexts.
Shorter prompts, moving speaker last, and repeating the current message at the end have mixed results; do not deploy these experimental formats based on cherry-picked successes.
changes_shipped: Remove cross-NPC wording examples and extra variety instructions on first attempt; keep session duplicate checks and bounded retry.
Describe activity keys in readable text and daily jobs as enum names; blank goal detail becomes unknown.
Direct questions receive the same queue grace as urgent events; ambient expiry remains short.
Discard obsolete answer/action if the same player has sent a newer queued message.
Log model readiness/configuration and shutdown counters without raw prompts.
recommendation: Use Qwen2.5 as the practical default for the current releases. There is no established quality gain justifying the current LFM3 CPU delay, and MiniCPM gains are inconsistent. Keep larger artifacts for research; do not delete automatically. Improve input/context diversity and grounding before retraining any tier.
next_training_experiment_not_executed: Keep ten distinct short replies per block, but add many distinct paraphrased inputs and counterfactual contexts: same job/inventory with unrelated questions; same question across different jobs/inventories.

Increase coherent two-turn follow-ups, corrections, NPC names, jobs and genuine unknown-state cases. Avoid contradictory acceptance/refusal labels under identical personality/context unless the ambiguity is deliberate.
Use paired held-out relevance/grounding cases and rendered live-style contexts for checkpoint selection. JSON validity/action accuracy/loss alone are not quality gates.

If continuing tier research, compare base/adapter/merged/GGUF outputs and several checkpoints/learning rates on the same held-out set before publishing; do not assume two epochs and one recipe suit all architectures.
